_meta.indication: TEGSEDI is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study CS2 (ISIS 420915-CS2), the single adequate and well-controlled pivotal trial
pivotal_trials.design: 66-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial conducted at 24 sites in 10 countries; patients randomized 2:1 to inotersen 284 mg SC weekly (recommended dosage per label; the review describes it on the salt basis as 300 mg doses following 3 loading doses in Week 1) or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18-82 years with hATTR amyloidosis with a documented TTR gene mutation and biopsy-documented amyloid deposition, Stage 1 or Stage 2 polyneuropathy, and baseline NIS of 10 to 130.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Week 66 in the modified Neuropathy Impairment Score+7 (mNIS+7) composite score and the Norfolk Quality of Life-Diabetic Neuropathy (QoL-DN) total score.
pivotal_trials.n: 173 patients enrolled; 172 patients randomized 2:1 to inotersen (N=113) or placebo (N=60).
pivotal_trials.result: Both co-primary endpoints significantly favored inotersen at Week 66: mNIS+7 LS mean treatment difference -19.7 [95% CI -26.4, -13.0], p<0.001; Norfolk QoL-DN LS mean treatment difference -11.7 [95% CI -18.3, -5.1], p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20% and more frequent than placebo) were injection site reactions, nausea, headache, fatigue, thrombocytopenia, and fever. Injection site reactions 49% vs 10%, nausea 31% vs 12%, thrombocytopenia 24% vs 2%. Serious risks include severe thrombocytopenia (platelet counts <100 x10^9/L in 25% vs 2%) and glomerulonephritis (occurred in 3% of TEGSEDI-treated patients vs no patient on placebo).
target_moa: Inotersen is a 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide that selectively binds to TTR mRNA, causing degeneration of both wild-type and mutant TTR mRNA and reducing serum TTR protein by an average of 70%.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Thrombocytopenia and Glomerulonephritis: TEGSEDI causes reductions in platelet count that may result in sudden, unpredictable, life-threatening thrombocytopenia (one trial patient died from intracranial hemorrhage); it can cause glomerulonephritis that may require immunosuppressive treatment and may result in dialysis-dependent renal failure. Both require prior testing and monitoring during treatment.

rems.type: TEGSEDI is available only through a restricted distribution program under a REMS (the TEGSEDI REMS Program) because of risks of serious bleeding caused by severe thrombocytopenia and because of glomerulonephritis, both of which require frequent monitoring.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for the lethal disease being treated.

summary.text: TEGSEDI (inotersen), an NME antisense oligonucleotide, received Orphan Drug Designation and Fast-Track Designation, and its original NDA was reviewed under Priority review, receiving traditional approval based on the single pivotal Study CS2. Approval included a REMS and postmarketing requirements; the application was not referred to an advisory committee.
